cohort: Singleton pregnant women, with a control group of pregnant women with three umbilical vessels or isolated single umbilical artery (iSUA)
finding: Abnormal umbilical cord insertion, preconception BMI, and thrombophilia were identified as risk factors for umbilical artery thrombosis (UAT), which itself was associated with higher risks of adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Pregnancies complicated by umbilical artery thrombosis had a higher risk of cesarean delivery compared to pregnancies with three umbilical vessels or isolated single umbilical artery.
